subtitle: Production-grade skills for AI coding agents

slides.title: agent-skills
slides.subtitle: Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents
slides.foot: What they are, and why they matter.

slides.text: AI coding agents default to the shortest path.
slides.sub: That usually means skipping specs, tests, and reviews. The practices that make software reliable are the first to go.

slides.heading: A skill is a workflow, not a prompt
bullets: Structured steps the agent follows, with checkpoints and exit criteria
An anti-rationalization table that rebuts the excuses to skip a step
Red flags that signal the process is being violated
Verification that demands evidence: tests, build output, runtime data

slides.heading: Every skill has the same shape
slides.caption: Frontmatter routes the work. The body is a process. Guardrails and proof are built in.

slides.heading: One command per phase, Define to Ship
slides.caption: 24 skills spanning the whole SDLC. The right ones load automatically for each phase.

slides.heading: Install into 70+ agents in one command
slides.sub: Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and more. Or add a single skill with --skill.

slides.heading: Start with a spec, then build
bullets: Run /spec to write a short PRD before any code
Run /build to implement in thin, tested slices
Every slice is committed and verified individually
You approve at each checkpoint. Nothing ships on vibes.

slides.title: Give your agent a senior engineer’s instincts
The SDLC, in practice
slides.subtitle: How you actually drive a feature from idea to production
slides.foot: Eight commands, six phases, one checkpoint at each step.

slides.heading: Eight commands map to the lifecycle
The daily loop
slides.caption: Install once. Drive each phase with a command. Repeat per feature.

slides.heading: Get the intent right before writing code
bullets: interview-me extracts what you actually want, one question at a time
spec-driven-development writes objectives, structure, tests, and boundaries
planning-and-task-breakdown turns the spec into small, ordered, verifiable tasks

slides.heading: Write it in slices, prove each one
bullets: incremental-implementation lands thin vertical slices, rollback-friendly
test-driven-development enforces red, green, refactor with a real test pyramid
Anti-rationalization tables stop "I will add tests later" before it happens
debugging-and-error-recovery finds the root cause instead of guessing

slides.heading: Gate on quality, then roll out
bullets: code-review-and-quality runs a five-axis review with severity labels
security-and-hardening applies OWASP Top 10 prevention and boundary checks
shipping-and-launch handles staged rollouts, monitoring, and rollback

slides.heading: Approve the plan once, let it run
slides.sub: Generates the plan and implements every task in one approved pass. Still test-driven, still committed per task, still pauses on failures.

slides.title: Drive the whole lifecycle with a checkpoint at each phase
Teams and customization
slides.subtitle: Scale the discipline across a team, and bend it to your stack
slides.foot: Review panels, context budgets, custom skills, and evals.

slides.heading: Ship past a panel, not a rubber stamp
slides.caption: /ship fans out to four specialist personas in parallel, then merges one go / no-go.

slides.heading: Four ways to make it yours
slides.caption: Install all, pick a few, edit them, or write your own. Skills are plain Markdown.

slides.heading: Load only what the task needs
bullets: More context is not better. Context is a budget you spend deliberately.
context-engineering configures rules files and packs the right information
Working on UI? Load frontend-ui-engineering. Debugging? Load the debugging skill.
The using-agent-skills meta-skill routes each task to the right workflow

slides.heading: The skills are measured, not asserted
bullets: A three-tier eval framework lives in the repo
Tier 1 checks structure. Tier 2 checks routing so no two skills collide.
Tier 3 grades a real execution trace against per-skill expectations
Some of it runs in CI, so regressions are caught early

slides.heading: One source of truth for the whole team
bullets: Commit your edited skills to version control
Every engineer and their agent share the same conventions
Spec and task artifacts are living documents during the work
New team members inherit the standards on day one

slides.title: Encode your team’s standards once. Every agent follows them.
